l4_steps.name: Monitor operational alerts for IRROP triggers
l4_steps.input: Flight delay or cancellation signals from ops control, ATC, or OCC
l4_steps.output: IRROP alert ticket created with flight number, delay code, and estimated passenger impact count
l4_steps.kpi: IRROP detection-to-alert time ≤15 min from event confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS integration with Altéa PSS can lag 5–10 min during high-volume events, widening the window before rebooking can begin and increasing downstream queue pressure

l4_steps.name: Classify disruption type, cause, and regulatory scope
l4_steps.input: IRROP alert from SITA AMS, IATA delay codes, flight status data
l4_steps.output: Disruption classification record (delay / cancel / divert), IATA cause code, DOT 14 CFR Part 250 and EC 261/2004 applicability flag
l4_steps.kpi: Cause code classification accuracy ≥95%; regulatory flag set within 5 min of classification
l4_steps.pain_point: Weather vs. technical cause code misclassification directly affects DOT compensation liability exposure; Altéa delay code mapping requires manual override when ops and commercial teams disagree

l4_steps.name: Activate IRROP protocol and notify stakeholders
l4_steps.output: IRROP case opened in Salesforce with severity tier; airport ops, crew coordination, and customer comms teams alerted
l4_steps.kpi: All operational stakeholders notified within 10 min of IRROP classification; case opened with correct priority tier in 100% of activations
l4_steps.pain_point: Parallel activation across Altéa, Salesforce, and the crew management system has no single handshake confirmation; coordination gaps emerge during simultaneous multi-flight IRROPs

l4_steps.name: Extract affected passenger manifest and PNR records
l4_steps.input: Disrupted flight number and departure date from IRROP case
l4_steps.output: Full passenger manifest with PNR, contact details (email, mobile), fare class, loyalty tier, and connection itinerary flag
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest extraction completed within 5 min of IRROP activation; contact data completeness ≥92% of affected PAX
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers booked through OTAs and GDS channels frequently have incomplete or agency-held contact fields in the Altéa PNR; direct SMS or email outreach fails for approximately 8% of affected passengers

l4_steps.name: Segment passengers by recovery priority tier
l4_steps.input: Passenger manifest with loyalty tier, fare basis, connection risk flag, and booking channel
l4_steps.output: Prioritised recovery queue: P1 (elite status and passengers with tight connections), P2 (connecting itineraries), P3 (point-to-point local)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of premium-tier and connection-at-risk passengers classified as P1 before notification dispatch
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa segmentation logic does not automatically identify passengers with connection windows under 60 min on the same PNR; analysts must manually review itineraries, adding 10–15 min per large event

l4_steps.name: Send proactive disruption notification with self-serve link
l4_steps.input: Prioritised passenger manifest, disruption details, self-service rebooking portal URL
l4_steps.output: SMS, email, and app push notification sent per passenger; self-service rebooking link and 60-minute response window communicated
l4_steps.kpi: ≥90% of affected PAX notified within 30 min of IRROP activation; self-serve rebooking adoption ≥35% of notified passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Push notification delivery drops to approximately 72% for passengers without the airline app installed; passengers booked via travel agencies require manual outreach via GDS telex, which averages 20 min per agency

l4_steps.name: Run automated rebooking engine against open inventory
l4_steps.input: Prioritised unresolved passenger queue, disrupted flight data, real-time seat inventory
l4_steps.output: Candidate alternative itineraries generated per passenger prioritised by departure proximity and cabin match
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-rebook match rate ≥70% of affected passengers on same-day service; engine execution time ≤3 min per 200-PAX event
l4_steps.pain_point: Inventory constraints on popular routes during a large IRROP cause cascading rebooking failures; Altéa auto-rebook does not dynamically reprice across fare classes without a manual IT change request, locking lower-fare passengers out of available premium inventory

l4_steps.name: Validate alternative itinerary against re-protection policy
l4_steps.input: Candidate itineraries, re-protection policy thresholds (same-day ±4 hrs; next-day ±24 hrs)
l4_steps.output: Policy-compliant itinerary approved for issuance, or case flagged for agent-assisted recovery
l4_steps.kpi: Re-protection policy compliance ≥98% of issued auto-rebooks; policy exception review completed within 5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Re-protection thresholds are hardcoded configuration parameters in Altéa requiring an IT change request to update; during major weather events affecting 50+ flights simultaneously the static thresholds cannot flex to match available capacity

l4_steps.name: Issue confirmed rebooking and send updated itinerary
l4_steps.output: Updated PNR with new flight segment, boarding pass where applicable, confirmation notification delivered via AWS SNS
l4_steps.kpi: Itinerary confirmation delivered within 5 min of rebooking commit; boarding pass pre-issuance success rate ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: DCS boarding pass pre-issuance fails for departures more than 24 hrs out or where gate assignment is pending at origin; passengers receive confirmation but must re-check in at the airport, creating service desk queue spikes

l4_steps.name: Assess passenger welfare entitlement under applicable regulations
l4_steps.input: Disruption cause code, flight distance, delay duration, passenger origin and nationality
l4_steps.output: Entitlement determination per DOT 14 CFR Part 250 and EC 261/2004; overnight flag, meal flag, and transport flag set on IRROP case
l4_steps.kpi: Entitlement determination completed within 15 min of IRROP activation; regulatory accuracy ≥99% validated by Customer Relations
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-regulation scenarios on transatlantic routes require manual legal review; Salesforce workflow rules do not auto-resolve cross-jurisdictional entitlement conflicts, exposing the airline to under-compensation claims and EU regulatory fines

l4_steps.name: Issue hotel accommodation vouchers for stranded passengers
l4_steps.input: Overnight entitlement flag, passenger count by airport, contracted hotel partner API availability
l4_steps.output: Hotel voucher codes issued digitally via app, email, or airport kiosk; rooms blocked with hotel partner
l4_steps.kpi: Hotel voucher issuance within 45 min of overnight determination; room availability confirmed for ≥90% of entitled passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotel partner API connectivity is inconsistent at smaller outstations; manual phone booking is required at approximately 30% of network stations, extending wait times to 2+ hrs and exhausting customer service staff capacity during simultaneous multi-station IRROPs

l4_steps.name: Distribute meal and ground transportation vouchers
l4_steps.input: Delay duration, regulatory entitlement thresholds, terminal and gate location
l4_steps.output: Meal vouchers and transport vouchers issued digitally or at service desk; voucher redemption records logged in SITA
l4_steps.kpi: ≥85% of vouchers issued digitally (app or email); airport service desk queue time ≤20 min during events under 300 PAX
l4_steps.pain_point: Digital voucher adoption varies significantly by passenger demographic; elderly and tech-averse passengers queue at service desks, creating bottlenecks during large IRROPs that overwhelm deployed airport staff ratios

l4_steps.name: Route unresolved cases to contact centre agent queue
l4_steps.input: IRROP cases with no auto-rebook match or passenger rejection of auto-offer
l4_steps.output: Cases assigned to agent queue with priority tier flag; estimated wait time communicated to passenger via SMS
l4_steps.kpi: P1 passengers reached by agent within 5 min; P2 within 15 min; P3 within 30 min of queue entry
l4_steps.pain_point: Contact centre surge during large IRROP events pushes wait times to 60–90 min for P3 passengers; AWS Connect IVR overflow routing is not dynamically linked to real-time IRROP case volume for on-demand agent staffing scale-up

l4_steps.name: Present interline and OAL rebooking options to passenger
l4_steps.input: Unresolved IRROP case, active interline e-ticketing agreements, OAL real-time availability
l4_steps.output: Expanded rebooking options including partner carrier itineraries presented and explained to passenger
l4_steps.kpi: Interline option presented within 10 min of agent engagement; OAL rebook success rate ≥60% when invoked
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline agreements and bilateral e-ticketing eligibility must be manually verified in Sabre before issuance; Altéa has no automated interline rebook capability for many partner carriers, requiring agents to switch between Sabre and Altéa and manually reissue tickets

l4_steps.name: Confirm passenger decision on rebooking or refund
l4_steps.input: Alternative itinerary options presented, passenger verbal or digital preference
l4_steps.output: Accepted rebooking confirmed in Altéa PNR, or refund request logged in Salesforce Service Cloud with case ID
l4_steps.kpi: Agent average handling time ≤12 min per case; passenger acceptance rate of presented alternatives ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: Refund processing for NDC-booked tickets falls outside the standard Altéa refund workflow; agents must manually process credits across 2–3 systems, extending handling time by 8–12 min per NDC case and increasing error rates

l4_steps.name: Calculate entitlement and initiate compensation payment
l4_steps.input: Confirmed refund or compensation decision, entitlement determination record, original fare paid
l4_steps.output: Refund or compensation payment initiated in SAP; payment timeline and reference communicated to passenger via Salesforce case
l4_steps.kpi: Refund processing completed within 7 business days per DOT requirement; compensation acknowledgement letter issued within 24 hrs of claim receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Refunds for GDS and OTA-booked tickets must route through the original selling channel; the airline has no direct refund path to the customer, requiring agency debit memos or manual credit card processing that can extend settlement to 15–30 business days

l4_steps.name: Log IRROP event data and capture NPS impact
l4_steps.input: Closed IRROP cases from Salesforce, post-event NPS survey responses, cost summary from SAP
l4_steps.output: IRROP event record with root cause, passenger count, recovery rate, NPS delta, and total recovery cost; stored in data lake for reporting
l4_steps.kpi: Post-IRROP NPS survey response rate ≥25%; recovery satisfaction score ≥3.5 out of 5.0; event record published within 48 hrs of case closure
l4_steps.pain_point: NPS survey responses from post-IRROP emails are not automatically linked to specific IRROP event records in Salesforce; manual tagging is required, delaying analytics availability by 48–72 hrs and reducing the accuracy of root cause attribution
